Lesson 048: authority models

    What this shows

    One fact, one decider

    If two machines may both decide who caught a fish, sooner or later they both say "me". Pick one owner for every piece of state that matters.

    Never trust the player's machine

    A modified client can say anything. Whoever decides catches must be a machine no player controls.

    Authority can be split

    The server owns fish and coins. Your phone owns your boat's steering, and the server only checks it is not too fast. You get both fairness and feel.

    This lab is a simulation, not a measurement. It uses Lesson 048's numbers: 100,000 players a day in 25,000 four-player sessions of 1 hour, 20 catches a player an hour (2,000,000 a day); 3% of catches are contested (two hooks on one fish less than 1 s apart); phone to phone 120 ms round trip (60 ms one way), phone to server 50 ms; 1 player in 200 runs a modified client; the host leaves early in 8% of sessions; relays $300 a month, dedicated servers $0.001 a player-hour (3,000,000 player-hours a month).
